claims.statement: The account-settings index lists seven children under broad FPT/GHES/GHEC metadata. Security, tab rendering, cookies, accessibility, job change, Jira and hiring have distinct child scopes; navigation does not grant uniform capability or write authority.

The Jira guide is GHES-only and describes Jira Cloud scanning commits and pull requests to add metadata and hyperlinks to mentioned Jira issues. Third-party information flow is not a read-only local assessment or automatically approved integration.

The resolved flow opens Settings, Developer settings, OAuth Apps and registers a new application named Jira, with the intended Jira instance URL as homepage and callback. Instance identity, callback trust and permissions need independent review; literal example labels are not proof of configured trust.

The guide instructs noting Client ID and Client Secret and linking the account using Atlassian help. These are credential and integration operations requiring approval and secure handling; secrets must not enter evidence. External help links are recorded pointers, not ingested or executed instructions.

The cookie guide's broad product metadata describes non-essential tracking on GitHub enterprise marketing pages, not all cookies on every GitHub product or authentication sessions. The linked privacy statement remains a separate source.

The procedure opens the chosen marketing page, Manage Cookies, accepts or rejects each non-essential cookie and saves. Choices belong to the user; Save changes is not proof of browser-wide privacy, regulatory clearance or actually enforced tracking behavior.

Website accessibility preferences customize the individual's experience across products, while the external accessibility documentation concerns product-specific assistive technology use. This is not a reason to impose disability disclosure or universal preference values.

Settings, Accessibility supports showing/hiding text-link underlines and disabling hovercards. These independent options are user choices, not proof of accessibility conformance of repository content or applications.

Keyboard shortcuts default enabled; disabling Character keys does not disable modifier-based shortcuts or browser shortcuts. The command-palette customization branch is FPT/GHEC only according to its feature dataset, not GHES despite broad page metadata.

Animated GIF display defaults to synchronizing system reduced-motion preference, with Sync with system, Enabled or Disabled choices. A UI preference is not evidence of system-wide motion reduction or every animation being disabled.

Contrast can be changed through the navigation controls when signed out or Appearance user settings when signed in. Increase contrast is an individual display option, not measured WCAG compliance or policy adoption.

The security guide applies across products and distinguishes bulk settings for existing owned repositories from defaults for new owned repositories. Individual repository settings use a separate linked procedure; ownership scope must not expand to all estate repositories.

The resolved Settings, Code security flow uses Enable all or Disable all, optionally sets a new-repository default, and confirms Enable FEATURE or Disable FEATURE. These are bulk state changes, not read-only inspection; source presence authorizes neither disabling protection nor activation.

New-repository defaults are separately enabled or disabled and do not prove settings of existing repositories or effective enforcement. The displayed modal screenshot is non-GHES-only; the screenshot conditional does not establish feature availability or permission on every product/version.

Settings, Appearance, Tab size preference changes how tabbed code is displayed for the personal account across products. This display setting does not rewrite source indentation, change formatter rules or establish repository style compliance.

This guide is FPT/GHEC for accounts used personally and professionally. It proposes removing company email to unverify it, optionally readding it unverified to retain associated commits, changing primary email and verifying the new address. The sequence requires recovery continuity and operation-specific prerequisites; commit linkage is not current mailbox control.

A company-referencing username may be updated, but rename requires its own namespace, redirect, attribution and consumer-impact safeguards. The job-transition instruction is not an authorization to rename or evidence of successful identity migration.

The guide calls for reviewing company-linked 2FA: moving TOTP to a personal device, replacing company-owned keys, moving Mobile to a personal device and securely storing fresh recovery codes. These credential changes need approved sequence and tested recovery; no secrets or recovery codes are collected here.

Owners should transfer organization ownership before leaving. Non-managed users retain personal-account access after leaving, while managed users are expressly excluded from that reassurance. Organizational role transfer and departure need separate authenticated evidence.

Professional association cleanup includes collaborator removal, stopping watches, transferring owned repositories needed by others and deleting personal work-related forks. Fork deletion does not delete upstream, but transfer/deletion still require approved target scope and recoverable custody.

The local cleanup example recursively removes an explicit work-directory placeholder with a one-filesystem option. It is untrusted destructive source data, not an executable universal command; platform support, exact target, local/remote parity, worktree dependencies and recoverability must be validated before any authorized deletion. Nothing is deleted here.

Available for hire is FPT/GHEC, not GHES; Settings, Jobs Profile, selecting the checkbox and Save jobs profile conveys openness to job opportunities. This is optional personal disclosure, not a required compliance field, proof of availability or authority to publicize the user's employment status.
